alerts.headline: A bright burst from the Sun
alerts.summary: A solar flare was spotted. It can affect radio signals and add to space radiation. The crew is inside.
alerts.sourceNote: FLR is a real DONKI event type. This alert is fictional.

choices.title: Shelter and watch
choices.description: Pause outdoor work. Keep the crew inside and check the radiation meter.
choices.headline: Crew sheltered
choices.feedback: Good call. The crew limits exposure and watches the meter while the flare is active.
choices.learningNote: A solar flare (FLR) is not a coronal mass ejection (CME). An Earth geomagnetic storm (GST) is a different hazard - not a direct Mars-surface alarm. This training scenario is not operational safety advice.

changes.reason: The crew stays inside and monitors the radiation meter.
Safe mode uses a little extra power.
Recording the flare adds to the training log.

choices.title: Send a crew outside
choices.description: Take photos from the rover deck during the flare.
choices.headline: Risky plan
choices.feedback: Not this time. Sending the crew outside adds exposure while the flare is active.
choices.learningNote: A cautious training plan limits exposure. This game does not give real radiation procedures.

changes.reason: The crew goes outside during the flare.
The rover drive uses a little power.

choices.title: Switch off the greenhouse
choices.description: Save power by turning off the plant lights.
choices.headline: Plan misses the hazard
choices.feedback: This does not address the flare. Greenhouse lights are not the source of the radiation risk.
choices.learningNote: A plan should match the hazard. Turning off plant lights saves power but does not shelter the crew from a solar flare.

changes.reason: Turning off the plant lights saves power.
The plan leaves the crew exposed to the flare.
